What can we make our robotic arm do?

If our robotic arm is simply controlled by joysticks, is it really a robot?

What if we can “program” the movements into it, and let it move on it’s own?
What Is EEPROM?
Permanent memory you can write from code — keeps its data even after the Arduino is unplugged.
Fast to read and write
Erased when power is turned off
Like a whiteboard: easy to change, but wiped every night
Survives power off and reboot
Limited writes (~100,000 per address)
Like a notebook: keeps notes even after you close it
#include <EEPROM.h>    // built-in, no install
EEPROM.put(address, data);  // save data at address
EEPROM.get(address, data);  // read data from address
Step 1: Save Positions (Button Press)
Each button press saves all 5 servo positions as one "frame" in EEPROM.
Count
How many frames saved
Frame 1
5 servo positions (10 bytes)
Frame 2
5 more positions
Frame 3
...and so on
if (joy1_btn == 0) {

  // Save count to address 0
  EEPROM.put(0, ee_size);

  // Save pos[] array
  EEPROM.put(ee_address, pos);

  ee_size += 1;
  ee_address += 10;  // 5 ints x 2 bytes
  while (joy1_btn ==0) {
     joy1_btn = digitalRead(JOY1_BUTTON_PIN);
     delay 50; 
  }

}
Each int is 2 bytes. 5 servo positions = 10 bytes per frame. The address jumps by 10 each time.
Step 2: Replay Saved Movements
Read each saved frame and walk every servo to its target — one degree at a time.
Read ee_size from EEPROM
Reset address to 2 (skip count)
For each saved frame:
load 5 positions from EEPROM
walk each servo to its target
bump address by 10 bytes
if (joy4.btn.pressed) {
  EEPROM.get(EE_SIZE_ADDRESS, ee_size);
  ee_address = 2;
  for (int i=0; i<ee_size; i++) {
    EEPROM.get(ee_address, new_pos);
    for (int j=0; j<5; j++) {
      while (pos[j] > new_pos[j]) {
        pos[j]--; arm_servos[j].write(pos[j]);
        delay(50); }
      while (pos[j] < new_pos[j]) {
        pos[j]++; arm_servos[j].write(pos[j]);
        delay(50); }
    }
    ee_address += 10;
  }
}
Two while loops nudge each servo down or up by one degree, with a tiny delay(50) — that pause is what makes the motion look smooth.
